overview: Albania is a country in the Balkans, on the eastern shores of the Adriatic and Ionian seas. Its capital and largest city is Tirana. Albania was ruled by the Ottoman Empire for more than four centuries and declared independence in 1912. After decades of strict communist rule that cut it off from much of the world, it became a multi-party democracy in the early 1990s, and it joined NATO in 2009.

geography.text: Most of Albania is mountainous, with the Albanian Alps in the north and long ranges running down the country. A strip of coastal plain lies along the Adriatic, while the south faces the Ionian Sea. Albania shares three large lakes with its neighbours: Lake Shkodër with Montenegro, Lake Ohrid with North Macedonia, and Lake Prespa with North Macedonia and Greece.

history.text: Albania's lands were part of the Roman and Byzantine empires before the Ottomans took control in the 1400s, despite fierce resistance led by the national hero Skanderbeg. Albania declared independence in 1912. After the Second World War, Enver Hoxha's communist government cut the country off from almost the whole world for four decades, until protests brought multi-party democracy in the early 1990s.

events.title: Skanderbeg dies
events.text: He had held off Ottoman armies for 25 years; more than four centuries of Ottoman rule followed.

events.title: Independence declared
events.text: Albania declares independence from the Ottoman Empire in the port of Vlorë.

events.title: Communists take power
events.text: Enver Hoxha begins four decades of hard-line, isolated rule.

events.title: First free elections
events.text: Multi-party elections follow the fall of communism.

events.title: Joins NATO
events.text: Albania becomes a member of the NATO alliance.
